correctness.rationale: PASS — For P=Q×[-1,1], antipodality of two distinct points is equivalent to their difference lying on ∂((Q−Q)×[-2,2]). Thus every different-layer vertex pair qualifies (n²), and same-layer pairs reduce to n+p(Q) planar antipodal pairs per layer. Rotating support normals count the latter with two additional cross-endpoint pairs for each opposite-parallel edge pair. Edge midpoints split disjointly into horizontal/horizontal opposite layers n², horizontal/horizontal same layer 2p, vertical/vertical n+p, horizontal/vertical 2n+4p; hence B=n²+3n+7p, A=n²+2n+2p, δ=3n−1+5p. Affine invertibility preserves support and midpoint structure. Direct independent integer difference-body hull tests for triangle, generic quadrilateral, trapezoid, rectangle and centrally symmetric hexagon reproduced (n,p,A,B,δ)=(3,0,15,18,8),(4,0,24,28,11),(4,1,26,35,16),(4,2,28,42,21),(6,3,54,75,32). No finite examples replace the rotating-support argument.
